reviewed_by: Cline (applying the domain review notes to the machine-reviewed file)
notes: Merge of edited_ontology.json (source=llm-review) with the review-application fixes: duplicate entry names removed, one-way edges closed, formulation outputs completed, urea re-homed, the fuel-oil -> carbon-black edge dropped (it leaked tire makers into fuel-oil research), and the notes' unimplemented items resolved: added polythene + aqueous ammonia HS codes, sulphur/phosphate-rock feedstocks, phosgene as the chlorine -> isocyanate bridge, and two value-chain leaves (plastics converting, pulp and paper). Declined with reasons: a bare 'peroxide' alias (matches benzoyl/cumene peroxide), cat:organic-acids (would fragment the ester/acid taxonomy; acrylic and acetic acid sit in chemical-intermediates), and proc:oxidation (a generic reaction with no operator vocabulary). Still pending a human domain expert: every node remains status=proposed.

sub:phosgene.label: Phosgene
sub:phosgene.expert_note: Bridge node: chlorine is the feedstock, phosgene the intermediate, isocyanates the product. Without it chlorine appeared to convert straight into TDI/MDI.

end:plastics-converting.label: Plastics converting
end:plastics-converting.expert_note: Closes the polyethylene/polypropylene/polystyrene dead ends: without it those commodities reached no end-user leaf.

cat:soap.expert_note: Dropped the 'soap noodles' alias: the commodity node sub:soap-noodles now owns that entry name, and one name must resolve to one node.

cat:fatty-alcohols.expert_note: Dropped the 'fatty alcohol' alias: sub:fatty-alcohol is the commodity and owns the singular name.

sub:fuel-oil.expert_note: Dropped derived_to sub:carbon-black: carbon-black feedstock is normally FCC slurry or decant oil, not fuel oil, and the edge surfaced tire manufacturers as end users of fuel-oil blending.

end:metalworking-fluids.expert_note: Renamed the 'coolants' alias to 'metalworking coolants': end:coolants-antifreeze owns engine/heat-transfer coolants, and the bare word was ambiguous.

sub:urea.expert_note: Organic carbamide made from ammonia and CO2 (HS chapter 31, not 28). Homed under organic chemical intermediates rather than petrochemicals, which is where the reviewed file put it.
